changes: No substantive changes. I expanded the note on dating: the colophon says only 'saṃ', and the date is read as Nepal Saṃvat.

notes: The colophon gives only 'saṃ 850' with no era name. The catalogue has 'VS 850', which would be about 793 CE. That is implausible for a paper manuscript in Newari script. Read as Nepal Saṃvat, NS 850 is about 1730 CE (Phālguna, February/March 1730). This is the usual reading of a bare three-digit 'saṃ' in Newari-script colophons. The weekday (Thursday) has not been checked against an ephemeris. The colophon ends the Anudyūtaparvan section of the Sabhāparvan ('77' is a section/chapter number).
